settings.heading: Details
settings.content:
Three ingredients, three jobs. Beeswax (true breathable barrier), virgin coconut oil (medium-chain fatty acids that nourish), unrefined red palm oil (vitamin E and tocotrienols).

No lanolin, no synthetic flavoring, no numbing agents. The chronic-chap problem we usually trace to one of those three.

Honest trade-off. Firmer than a drugstore balm because beeswax sets harder than the waxes they use. Apply with light pressure rather than a smear.

settings.title: Organic Beeswax
settings.text: Moisture-lock barrier. Beeswax forms a breathable film on the lips that holds moisture in without sealing the lips shut. Its long-chain fatty acids and esters give the balm its stick structure and let it stay put through wear. The waxes most balms use are cheaper and more occlusive — we chose beeswax because the lips can still exchange.

settings.title: Organic Virgin Coconut Oil
settings.text: Nourishing fatty acid base. Cold-pressed virgin coconut oil delivers medium-chain fatty acids — roughly half of which is lauric acid — into the thin skin of the lips. Where a barrier wax sits on top, virgin coconut oil absorbs and feeds. Refined coconut oil is cheaper and more uniform, but the deodorizing process strips out the lauric acid that does the work.

settings.title: Organic Red Palm Oil
settings.text: Vitamin E and beta-carotene source. Unrefined red palm oil delivers naturally occurring vitamin E and tocotrienols to the thin skin of the lips — antioxidants that support tissue health where it shows fastest. The deep red-orange color is the carotenoids themselves. RSPO-certified sourcing.

We started Real Skin Care because our family wanted products where we could confirm every ingredient. With lip balm, that meant flipping over the tube and asking why paraffin and undisclosed flavoring were in something we put on our kids' lips every day.

We took it down to three ingredients that each do real work, and we won't compromise that for cost.

— Sean Fillmore

settings.heading: Why does this balm feel firmer than the lip balm I'm used to?
settings.row_content: Beeswax sets harder than petroleum-based waxes like paraffin and microcrystalline wax. Apply with light pressure rather than a smear, and let the warmth of your lips soften the layer into place. After a few seconds it spreads easily. The trade-off for the firmer set is a balm that stays on the lips through wear instead of wiping off in minutes.

settings.heading: Why no lanolin? Most natural balms use it.
settings.row_content: Lanolin is a common allergen and a frequent driver of the chronic-chap problem this balm is designed to solve. Customers who've tracked their chapping back to a previous balm often find lanolin in the ingredient list. We use beeswax for the barrier role and skip lanolin entirely so this balm works for sensitive lips that have reacted to it before.

settings.heading: Why doesn't the unscented version smell like nothing?
settings.row_content: The Pure Unscented variation has the natural scent of beeswax and coconut oil — that's what those ingredients smell like. Unscented means no added essential oils, not an absence of scent. A truly odorless balm requires deodorized, refined oils, and the deodorizing process strips out the fatty acids and antioxidants that make the formula work.

settings.heading: What's the light color in the variations from?
settings.row_content: Unrefined red palm oil. It's naturally red-orange because of its beta-carotene content — the same antioxidant that makes the oil worth using. Refined palm oil is bleached white and stripped of carotenes. The light tint you see in the tube is the carotenoids in their natural form, not added pigment.

settings.heading: Will this balm melt in a hot car or my pocket?
settings.row_content: Beeswax has a higher melt point than petroleum waxes, so the balm holds its shape better in heat than most. That said, prolonged exposure to direct sun or a hot car can soften any natural balm. If it softens, let it cool upright — the ingredients are unchanged, only the texture shifts. Coconut oil also firms up below 76°F.

settings.heading: Why no menthol or cooling sensation?
settings.row_content: The cooling sensation in commercial balms is produced by menthol mildly irritating the lips so they feel "treated." That irritation is exactly what sensitive lips don't need. We left menthol out. The lips feel softer and more comfortable because the barrier is intact and the skin underneath is being fed — not because something on the surface is signaling a sensation.

settings.heading: How is this different from the "natural" lip balms at the drugstore?
settings.row_content: Many balms labeled natural still contain paraffin, lanolin, or "natural flavor" listed as one word — a regulatory umbrella that can hide dozens of compounds. Our ingredient list is three base ingredients plus named essential oils where applicable. Each ingredient is on the label by its specific name, so you can verify what you're putting on your lips.

settings.heading: Is the red palm oil sustainably sourced?
settings.row_content: Yes — we use RSPO-certified red palm oil. The Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil certifies the palm comes from operations meeting strict standards: no deforestation, no peatland conversion, fair labor. The "red" matters too — refined palm oil is cheaper but the refining strips out the carotenoids and tocotrienols we use it for. Unrefined keeps the antioxidants intact.
